title.narrative: Provision of cash assistance for shelter and NFIs to vulnerable households affected by floods in Yen Bai Province

description.narrative: This project focuses on addressing the immediate needs of the affected population in Yen Bai, one of the provinces hardest hit by Typhoon Yagi. The typhoon caused severe damage, with 2,271 homes affected and over 22,442 houses flooded as of 20 September. The primary objective of this CERF-funded project is to enable the most vulnerable households to safely reside in their homes. To achieve this, the project will provide both multi-purpose unconditional cash assistance for immediate relief and conditional cash assistance to support home repairs, targeting a total of 2,060 households (approximately 7,840 people). Emergency shelter assistance will prioritize households whose homes were approximately 30 per cent damaged, focusing on those who can quickly return. Priority will be given to poor and near-poor households as well as well as households with members who have disabilities during the 2022-2024 period. Multi-purpose cash assistance could be used to purchase gender and disability-responsive non-food items, such as blankets, clothing, mosquito nets, cooking utensils, tools, and furniture, specific items for people with restricted mobility, visually impaired; all of which are supplemented by guidance to ensure these items can be used effectively to address basic needs and improve living conditions. Additionally, this cash assistance is expected to stimulate local markets, whose access and operations, were impacted by the typhoon. The project pays particular attention to the vulnerabilities and needs of poor women, women-headed households and people with disabilities. This inclusive design will ensure that recovery efforts are responsive, equitable, sustainable, and culturally appropriate, supporting long-term resilience for vulnerable populations. In addition, the emergency shelter assistance will ensure that people can repair and make their houses safe, considering the current winter conditions, which will worsen the situation, with expected cold spells and rainfall in the next three months. Emergency accommodations in local communities, often provided in neighbors' homes or public buildings like schools and health centers, place additional strain on social infrastructure. The project will help ease this pressure by repairing damaged homes and therefore contribute to ensuring continued access to education, healthcare, and other essential services.Global best practices emphasize that shelter assistance should be flexible and tailored to local social, cultural, and climatic conditions, as well as the scale of the disaster. In Viet Nam, lessons learned from UNDP’s CERF’s funded emergency responses to the previous storms in 2017, and in 2020 indicate that shelter kits, materials for home repairs, and unconditional cash support are among the most effective methods for delivering rapid shelter solutions. This project is built on these insights. With its extensive experience in building climate-resilient homes and in previous CERF-funded projects, UNDP will offer direct technical support and guidance to the local partners in Yen Bai province, to assist households in repairing their homes. As UNDP is already present in the targeted location, existing working relationships with local partners (including the local chapter of the Vietnamese Red Cross and the Women’s Union) and the provincial People’s Committees (PPC) will contribute to fast-tracking administrative procedures, selecting beneficiaries, and delivering time-sensitive activities on the ground.
